note: Drawing data for scripts/fitness-images.py (stream 07). One entry per registry exercise id: what the picture must show (machine as set up, setup, START/END, the arrow's path, the hardest point for the side view, camera override, fallback muscles and equipment). When content/fitness/exercises.json exists its name, equipment, muscles, setup and cues are used too; this file stays the source of the drawing directions. Text fields have no trailing full stop; the script adds punctuation.

cameras.three-quarter front: three-quarter front view: the camera stands in front of the mannequin and about 45 degrees to its left, at chest height, so the chest, both arms and the handles are all visible
cameras.three-quarter rear: three-quarter rear view: the camera stands behind the mannequin and about 45 degrees to its left, so the back of the shoulders and the upper back are visible
cameras.pure side: pure side (profile) view: the camera looks at the mannequin's left side at exactly 90 degrees to the direction it faces, so the mannequin is seen in profile facing the right side of the picture, with one arm and one leg in front and the other mostly hidden behind them; never a front, back or three-quarter view
cameras.high side: side view from the mannequin's left and slightly above, so the mannequin lying on the bench, the bar or dumbbells and their path are all visible
cameras.front: straight front view, the camera facing the mannequin at chest height
cameras.close-up: close-up three-quarter view of one forearm and hand only, filling the panel
cameras.three-quarter front, away from the colum: three-quarter front view from the side away from the cable column: the camera stands in front of the mannequin and about 45 degrees to its LEFT, at chest height; the cable column stands at the mannequin's RIGHT side, at the right edge of the picture and a little behind the mannequin, so the cable runs from the column across to the hands and the direction the chest faces points toward the lower left of the picture

horizontal-push.end: arms extended forward, elbows almost straight

incline-push.end: arms pressed up and forward along the incline
incline-push.path: up and forward along the incline

decline-push.start: hands at the lower chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees
decline-push.end: arms pressed down and forward, elbows almost straight
decline-push.path: down and forward from the lower chest

vertical-push.start: hands at shoulder height, elbows bent below the hands

chest-fly.start: arms open wide at chest height, elbows softly bent
chest-fly.end: hands brought together in front of the chest
chest-fly.path: an inward arc at chest height

vertical-pull.end: hands pulled down to the upper chest, elbows down beside the ribs
vertical-pull.path: straight down to the upper chest

horizontal-pull.start: arms extended forward, shoulder blades spread
horizontal-pull.end: hands pulled to the lower ribs, elbows behind the torso

pullover.end: arms swept down to the thighs
pullover.path: a downward arc around the shoulders

rear-delt.start: arms straight out in front at shoulder height
rear-delt.end: arms swept out to the sides at shoulder height
rear-delt.path: an outward arc at shoulder height

lateral-raise.end: arms raised out to the sides to shoulder height
lateral-raise.path: upward arcs out to the sides

front-raise.start: arms in front of the thighs
front-raise.end: arms raised forward to shoulder height

external-rotation.start: forearm across the belly, elbow at the side
external-rotation.end: forearm rotated outward, elbow still at the side
external-rotation.path: an outward arc around the elbow

elbow-flexion.end: elbows fully bent, upper arms unmoved
elbow-flexion.path: an upward arc around the elbows

forearm-flexion.path: a small arc around the wrists

forearm-extension.path: a small arc around the wrists

grip.path: a short arc beside the hand

trunk-flexion.end: torso curled forward, ribs toward the pelvis
trunk-flexion.path: a forward arc of the chest

anti-extension.end: body a long straight line, hips not sagging

anti-rotation.end: arms pressed straight out, torso square

lateral-flexion.end: hips raised into a straight side line

hip-flexion.path: an upward arc of the knees

spinal-extension.end: torso raised in line with the hips
spinal-extension.path: an upward arc of the torso

hip-hinge.start: hips back, torso hinged forward, back flat
hip-hinge.path: straight up close to the legs

squat.start: hips and knees bent, thighs about parallel

lunge.start: front thigh about parallel, back knee low

knee-flexion.path: an arc of the heels around the knees

knee-extension.path: an arc of the shins around the knees

carry.path: a straight arrow low beside the feet in the walking direction

neck.path: a small arc of the head

hip-extension.end: hips extended in line with the torso
hip-extension.path: an upward arc of the hips

muscles.pec-clavicular: the upper chest: the top part of the pectoralis major just below the collarbone
muscles.pec-sternal: the mid chest: the large fan-shaped pectoralis major from the breastbone to the front of the armpit
muscles.pec-costal: the lower chest: the lowest band of the pectoralis major along the bottom edge of the chest
muscles.serratus-anterior: the serratus: the finger-like strip on the side of the ribcage below the armpit
muscles.lats: the lats: the broad sheets on both sides of the back from under the armpits down to the lower back (from the side, the band under the armpit along the side of the ribcage)
muscles.teres-major: the teres major: the small thick muscle at the lower outer edge of the shoulder blade, at the back of the armpit
muscles.rhomboids: the rhomboids: between the shoulder blades and the spine
muscles.traps-upper: the upper trapezius: the slope between the neck and the shoulder
muscles.traps-mid: the middle trapezius: across the upper back between the shoulder blades
muscles.traps-lower: the lower trapezius: the lower point of the diamond running from between the shoulder blades down to the mid-back
muscles.delt-front: the front deltoid: the front of the shoulder
muscles.delt-side: the side deltoid: the outside cap of the shoulder
muscles.delt-rear: the rear deltoid: the back of the shoulder
muscles.rotator-cuff: the rotator cuff: the back of the shoulder blade below its ridge
muscles.biceps: the biceps: the front of the upper arm
muscles.brachialis: the brachialis: the outer front of the upper arm just above the elbow, beside the biceps
muscles.triceps-long: the triceps long head: the inner back of the upper arm running up into the armpit
muscles.triceps-lateral: the triceps lateral head: the outer back of the upper arm
muscles.forearm-flexors: the forearm flexors: the palm side of the forearm
muscles.forearm-extensors: the forearm extensors: the back-of-the-hand side of the forearm
muscles.brachioradialis: the brachioradialis: the thumb-side top of the forearm just below the elbow
muscles.rectus-abdominis: the rectus abdominis: the strip down the front of the belly from the ribs to the pelvis
muscles.obliques: the obliques: the sides of the waist between the ribs and the hip
muscles.transverse-abdominis: the deep abdominal corset: the lower belly and the waist
muscles.erectors: the spinal erectors: the two long columns either side of the spine in the lower and middle back
muscles.quadratus-lumborum: the quadratus lumborum: the deep lower back at the sides of the spine just above the pelvis
muscles.glute-med: the gluteus medius: the upper outer hip just below the rim of the pelvis
muscles.quads: the quadriceps: the front of the thigh
muscles.hip-flexors: the hip flexors: the front of the hip crease at the top of the thigh
muscles.hamstrings: the hamstrings: the back of the thigh
muscles.gastrocnemius: the gastrocnemius: the upper calf, the two bulging heads at the back of the lower leg
muscles.soleus: the soleus: the lower calf under the gastrocnemius, down to the Achilles tendon
muscles.adductors: the adductors: the inner thigh of BOTH legs (the left and the right, mirror images)
muscles.neck-flexors: the neck flexors: the front and sides of the neck
muscles.neck-extensors: the neck extensors: the back of the neck

cover: A quiet, clean corner of a small modern gym in soft warm morning light, seen at eye level from a gentle three-quarter angle: on the left a seated chest press machine (upright cream back pad, two horizontal handles on lever arms, a plain weight stack), in the middle a tall dual-pulley cable station with two weight stacks and a stirrup handle hanging from each pulley, on the right a lat pulldown station (tall frame, high pulley, a long bar on the cable, a seat with padded knee rollers, a weight stack); dark graphite frames, cream pads, light grey plates; a small pale-wood bench with a folded terracotta-orange towel on it; a warm grey rubber floor; a pale wall with one large window letting in warm ivory daylight that casts long soft shadows. Uncluttered, tidy and inviting. No people, no mirrors with reflections, no posters, nothing written anywhere: the weight stacks are plain plates without numbers, and there are no logos or brand names

machine-chest-press.name: Seated chest press machine
machine-chest-press.machine: a seated pin-loaded chest press: an upright padded back rest, an adjustable seat, two lever arms (one on each side of the seat, pivoting high on the frame behind the shoulders) that each end in a horizontal handle beside the chest and swing forward with the hands, and a weight stack with a selector pin standing behind the seat; nothing crosses in front of the chest
machine-chest-press.setup: seat height set so the handles are level with the middle of the chest; feet flat on the floor; hips, upper back and head against the back pad; a full grip on the horizontal handles with straight wrists
machine-chest-press.start: hands on the handles beside the chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees and slightly below shoulder height, upper arms about 45 degrees out from the torso, chest up, shoulder blades back against the pad
machine-chest-press.end: arms extended straight forward, handles pushed away to arm's length at mid-chest height, elbows almost straight but not locked, shoulder blades and head still on the pad
machine-chest-press.path: from the handles beside the chest straight forward to arm's length
machine-chest-press.hard: the bottom of the press: handles beside the middle of the chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees and just below shoulder height, upper arms level with the back pad, chest up, back and head on the pad

converging-chest-press.name: Converging chest press machine
converging-chest-press.machine: a seated pin-loaded converging chest press: an upright back pad, an adjustable seat, two independent handle arms that swing forward and inward on angled pivots so the hands meet in front of the chest, a weight stack beside the seat
converging-chest-press.setup: seat set so the handles are level with the middle of the chest; feet flat; back and head against the pad
converging-chest-press.start: hands on the handles beside the chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees and slightly below shoulder height
converging-chest-press.end: arms extended forward and inward, hands almost meeting in front of the breastbone, elbows nearly straight
converging-chest-press.path: forward and inward in a gentle arc from beside the chest to in front of the breastbone

plate-loaded-chest-press.name: Plate-loaded chest press
plate-loaded-chest-press.machine: a plate-loaded iso-lateral chest press: a heavy steel frame with a slightly reclined back pad and a seat, two independent lever arms with vertical handles that pivot from above and behind, round weight plates on a horn on each lever arm, no weight stack
plate-loaded-chest-press.setup: seat set so the handles are level with the middle of the chest; feet flat; back and head on the pad; neutral grip on the vertical handles
plate-loaded-chest-press.start: hands on the handles beside the chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees
plate-loaded-chest-press.end: both arms pressed forward to almost straight, the lever arms swung forward
plate-loaded-chest-press.path: forward and slightly downward in an arc from beside the chest to arm's length

smith-bench-press.name: Smith machine bench press
smith-bench-press.machine: a Smith machine: a barbell fixed on two vertical steel guide rails inside a tall frame, with rack hooks and adjustable safety stops, and a flat bench placed inside it so the bar comes down over the middle of the chest
smith-bench-press.setup: lying on the flat bench inside the Smith machine, eyes under the bar, feet flat on the floor, shoulder blades pulled back; hands on the bar a little wider than the shoulders
smith-bench-press.start: bar lowered to touch the middle of the chest, forearms vertical, elbows about 45 to 60 degrees out from the torso
smith-bench-press.end: bar pressed straight up along the rails to arm's length above the chest, elbows almost straight
smith-bench-press.path: straight up along the guide rails from the chest to arm's length

dumbbell-bench-press.name: Dumbbell bench press
dumbbell-bench-press.setup: lying on a flat bench, feet flat on the floor, shoulder blades pulled back, a dumbbell in each hand
dumbbell-bench-press.start: dumbbells at the sides of the chest, forearms vertical, elbows about 45 degrees out from the torso
dumbbell-bench-press.end: dumbbells pressed up over the chest to arm's length, close together but not touching
dumbbell-bench-press.path: straight up and slightly inward from the chest to arm's length

barbell-bench-press.name: Barbell bench press
barbell-bench-press.setup: lying on a flat bench with rack uprights, eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pulled back; hands a little wider than the shoulders
barbell-bench-press.start: bar lowered to touch the middle of the chest, forearms vertical
barbell-bench-press.end: bar pressed up to arm's length over the shoulders, elbows almost straight
barbell-bench-press.path: up and slightly back from the chest to above the shoulders

push-up.name: Push-up
push-up.setup: hands on the floor a little wider than the shoulders, body one straight line from head to heels, on the toes
push-up.start: chest lowered to a fist's height above the floor, elbows bent and about 45 degrees out from the torso
push-up.end: arms straight, body still one straight line
push-up.path: the chest rises straight up while the body pivots on the toes

machine-incline-press.name: Incline chest press machine
machine-incline-press.machine: a seated pin-loaded incline chest press: a back pad reclined about 30 to 45 degrees, an adjustable seat, two handles on lever arms that travel up and forward along the incline, a weight stack behind
machine-incline-press.setup: seat set so the handles start level with the upper chest just below the collarbones; feet flat; back and head on the reclined pad
machine-incline-press.start: hands on the handles beside the upper chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees and below the hands
machine-incline-press.end: arms extended up and forward along the incline, elbows almost straight, shoulders down
machine-incline-press.path: up and forward along the incline from the upper chest to arm's length
machine-incline-press.hard: the bottom of the press: handles beside the upper chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees, upper arms level with the back pad, back and head on the reclined pad

plate-loaded-incline-press.name: Plate-loaded incline press
plate-loaded-incline-press.machine: a plate-loaded iso-lateral incline press: a back pad reclined about 30 to 45 degrees, a seat, two independent lever arms with handles that press up and forward, weight plates on a horn on each lever arm
plate-loaded-incline-press.setup: seat set so the handles start at the upper chest; feet flat; back on the pad
plate-loaded-incline-press.start: hands on the handles beside the upper chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees
plate-loaded-incline-press.end: arms pressed up and forward to almost straight
plate-loaded-incline-press.path: up and forward in an arc from the upper chest

smith-incline-press.name: Smith machine incline press
smith-incline-press.machine: a Smith machine with an adjustable bench set to about 30 degrees incline inside it, so the bar comes down to the upper chest
smith-incline-press.setup: lying back on the 30-degree incline bench, feet flat, shoulder blades back; hands a little wider than the shoulders
smith-incline-press.start: bar lowered to the upper chest just below the collarbones, forearms vertical
smith-incline-press.end: bar pressed straight up along the rails to arm's length
smith-incline-press.path: straight up along the rails from the upper chest

incline-dumbbell-press.name: Incline dumbbell press
incline-dumbbell-press.setup: lying back on a bench set to about 30 degrees incline, feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand
incline-dumbbell-press.start: dumbbells at the sides of the upper chest, forearms vertical
incline-dumbbell-press.end: dumbbells pressed up over the upper chest to arm's length
incline-dumbbell-press.path: straight up from the upper chest to arm's length

incline-barbell-press.name: Incline barbell press
incline-barbell-press.setup: lying back on an incline bench of about 30 degrees with rack uprights, feet flat; hands a little wider than the shoulders
incline-barbell-press.start: bar lowered to the upper chest just below the collarbones
incline-barbell-press.end: bar pressed up to arm's length above the shoulders
incline-barbell-press.path: up from the upper chest to above the shoulders

low-to-high-cable-fly.name: Low-to-high cable fly
low-to-high-cable-fly.machine: a dual-pulley cable crossover station: two tall columns, each with a weight stack and an adjustable pulley carriage set at the LOWEST position, a single stirrup handle on each cable
low-to-high-cable-fly.setup: standing in the middle between the two low pulleys in a short split stance, a stirrup handle in each hand, palms facing forward and up
low-to-high-cable-fly.start: arms down and out to the sides below hip height, elbows softly bent, a stretch across the chest
low-to-high-cable-fly.end: hands swept up and together in front of the upper chest at about chin height, elbow bend unchanged
low-to-high-cable-fly.path: an upward and inward arc from beside the hips to in front of the upper chest, its head pointing at the middle of the upper chest

triceps-press-machine.name: Seated dip machine (triceps press)
triceps-press-machine.machine: a seated pin-loaded dip machine (triceps press): an upright back pad, a seat with a padded thigh hold-down, two handles beside the hips on lever arms that are pushed downward, a weight stack behind
triceps-press-machine.setup: seat set so the handles start level with the lower chest; back against the pad, thighs under the pad; neutral grip on the handles at the sides
triceps-press-machine.start: elbows bent about 90 degrees and pointing back, hands beside the lower ribs, shoulders down
triceps-press-machine.end: arms pressed straight down, hands beside the hips, elbows almost straight, torso upright against the pad
triceps-press-machine.path: straight down beside the body from the lower ribs to the hips
triceps-press-machine.hard: the start of the press: elbows bent about 90 degrees and pointing straight back, hands beside the lower ribs, shoulders down, torso upright against the pad

decline-chest-press-machine.name: Decline chest press machine
decline-chest-press-machine.machine: a seated pin-loaded decline chest press: an upright seat with a back pad, low handles on lever arms that travel forward and downward, a weight stack behind
decline-chest-press-machine.setup: seat set so the handles start level with the lower chest; feet flat; back on the pad
decline-chest-press-machine.start: hands on the handles beside the lower chest, elbows bent about 90 degrees
decline-chest-press-machine.end: arms extended forward and slightly downward, elbows almost straight
decline-chest-press-machine.path: forward and downward from the lower chest to arm's length

assisted-dip.name: Assisted dip
assisted-dip.machine: an assisted dip and chin-up machine: a tall frame with chin-up handles on top, parallel dip handles at hip height on both sides, and a padded knee platform on a lever linked to a weight stack that pushes up to help
assisted-dip.setup: kneeling on the assistance pad, hands on the parallel dip handles, torso leaning slightly forward
assisted-dip.start: elbows bent about 90 degrees, shoulders just above elbow height, torso leaning slightly forward
assisted-dip.end: arms pressed straight, body raised between the handles, shoulders down away from the ears
assisted-dip.path: the whole body rises straight up between the handles

dip.name: Parallel-bar dip
dip.setup: supported on parallel bars, arms straight, knees bent and ankles crossed behind
dip.start: elbows bent about 90 degrees, shoulders just above elbow height, torso leaning slightly forward
dip.end: arms pressed straight, body raised, shoulders down
dip.path: the whole body rises straight up between the bars

high-to-low-cable-fly.name: High-to-low cable fly
high-to-low-cable-fly.machine: a dual-pulley cable crossover station with both pulley carriages set HIGH, a single stirrup handle on each cable
high-to-low-cable-fly.setup: standing in the middle in a short split stance, leaning slightly forward, a stirrup handle in each hand
high-to-low-cable-fly.start: arms up and out to the sides above shoulder height, elbows softly bent, a stretch across the chest
high-to-low-cable-fly.end: hands swept down and together in front of the lower chest, elbow bend unchanged
high-to-low-cable-fly.path: a downward and inward arc from above the shoulders to in front of the lower chest, its head pointing at the middle of the lower chest

pec-deck.name: Pec deck (machine fly)
pec-deck.sideCamera: front view from slightly above: the camera in front of the seated mannequin and a little higher than its head, looking down at about 30 degrees, so the height of both arms and how far they open read clearly
pec-deck.machine: a seated pin-loaded pec deck (butterfly) machine: an upright back pad, an adjustable seat, two long swinging arms with vertical handles that swing together in front of the chest, a weight stack behind the seat
pec-deck.setup: seat set so the handles are at mid-chest height and the shoulders level with the arms' pivots; back and head against the pad; hands on the vertical handles, elbows softly bent
pec-deck.start: arms open wide to the sides at chest height, elbows softly bent and level with the back pad, a stretch across the chest
pec-deck.end: arms swept forward together so the handles nearly touch in front of the chest, elbow bend unchanged, back still on the pad
pec-deck.path: a curved arrow just above the hand on the right of the picture, starting at that open hand and curving inward toward the middle of the chest, its head pointing at the breastbone
pec-deck.hard: the open, stretched position: upper arms at chest height and in line with the back pad (not behind it), elbows softly bent about 20 degrees, chest up, back and head on the pad
pec-deck.sidePath: a curved arrow just above the hand on the right of the picture, starting at that open hand and curving inward toward the middle of the chest, its head pointing at the breastbone
pec-deck.sideNote: both arms open symmetrically at chest height, mirror images of each other; neither hand drops below the chest; the elbows are level with the back pad, not behind it

cable-fly.name: Cable fly
cable-fly.sideCamera: high front view: the camera in front of the mannequin and well above it, looking down at about 60 degrees, so both the height of the arms and how far they open behind the chest read clearly
cable-fly.machine: a dual-pulley cable crossover station: two tall columns, each with a weight stack and a pulley carriage set at shoulder height, a single stirrup handle on each cable
cable-fly.setup: standing centred between the columns in a short split stance, a slight forward lean, a handle in each hand, elbows softly bent
cable-fly.start: arms out to the sides at chest height, elbows softly bent, hands slightly behind the chest line, a stretch across the chest
cable-fly.end: hands brought together in front of the chest at chest height, elbow bend unchanged
cable-fly.path: one arrow beside each open hand, each starting at that hand and curving forward and inward toward the middle in front of the chest, the two heads pointing toward each other in front of the breastbone
cable-fly.hard: the open, stretched position: arms out to the sides at chest height with the hands just behind the chest line, elbows softly bent, slight forward lean, split stance
cable-fly.seqNote: both columns and their pulleys stay exactly the same in both panels, the pulleys at shoulder height; in both panels each cable runs from its own pulley straight to the handle in the hand on that side

dumbbell-fly.name: Dumbbell fly
dumbbell-fly.setup: lying on a flat bench, feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other, elbows softly bent
dumbbell-fly.start: arms open wide to the sides with the dumbbells level with the chest, elbows softly bent
dumbbell-fly.end: dumbbells brought together above the chest in a wide arc
dumbbell-fly.path: an upward arc from beside the chest to above it

machine-shoulder-press.name: Seated shoulder press machine
machine-shoulder-press.machine: a seated pin-loaded shoulder press: an upright back pad, an adjustable seat, two handles at shoulder height on lever arms that travel straight up, a weight stack behind
machine-shoulder-press.setup: seat set so the handles start level with the top of the shoulders; feet flat; back and head against the pad; palms facing forward on the handles
machine-shoulder-press.start: hands at shoulder height beside the head, elbows bent below the hands and slightly in front of the torso
machine-shoulder-press.end: arms pressed straight overhead, elbows almost straight, ribs down, back still on the pad
machine-shoulder-press.path: straight up from the shoulders to overhead
machine-shoulder-press.hard: the bottom of the press: handles level with the top of the shoulders, elbows bent below the hands and slightly in front of the torso, back flat on the pad
machine-shoulder-press.sideNote: the handles are at the height of the top of the shoulders, beside the ears — higher than the chin, never in front of the chest; the forearms are vertical with the elbows directly under the hands and a little below shoulder height; the lever arms come down from pivots above and behind the head; the handle in each hand is the lower end of its lever arm: the lever runs in one piece from its pivot above and behind the head down to the handle in the hand, so no handle floats

plate-loaded-shoulder-press.name: Plate-loaded shoulder press
plate-loaded-shoulder-press.machine: a plate-loaded shoulder press: a seat with an upright back pad, two independent lever arms with handles at shoulder height that press upward in an arc, weight plates on a horn on each lever arm
plate-loaded-shoulder-press.setup: seat set so the handles start level with the shoulders; feet flat; back on the pad
plate-loaded-shoulder-press.start: hands at shoulder height, elbows bent below the hands
plate-loaded-shoulder-press.end: arms pressed up overhead to almost straight
plate-loaded-shoulder-press.path: up in a slight arc from the shoulders to overhead
plate-loaded-shoulder-press.seqNote: the bright orange is ONLY on the shoulders — the round front and side deltoid caps where the arms join the body; the chest itself stays grey apart from, at most, a faint pale tint just under the collarbones

smith-shoulder-press.name: Smith machine shoulder press
smith-shoulder-press.machine: a Smith machine with an upright bench (back rest almost vertical) inside it, placed so the bar passes just in front of the face
smith-shoulder-press.setup: seated on the upright bench, back against the pad, feet flat; hands on the bar a little wider than the shoulders
smith-shoulder-press.start: bar at chin height just in front of the face, forearms vertical, elbows under the bar
smith-shoulder-press.end: bar pressed straight up along the rails to arm's length overhead
smith-shoulder-press.path: straight up along the rails from chin height to overhead

seated-dumbbell-shoulder-press.name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
seated-dumbbell-shoulder-press.setup: seated on a bench with the back rest upright, feet flat, a dumbbell in each hand
seated-dumbbell-shoulder-press.start: dumbbells at shoulder height beside the ears, palms forward, forearms vertical
seated-dumbbell-shoulder-press.end: dumbbells pressed overhead, arms almost straight, dumbbells close together
seated-dumbbell-shoulder-press.path: straight up from the shoulders to overhead

landmine-press.name: Landmine press
landmine-press.setup: standing in a staggered stance facing the free end of a barbell whose other end sits in a pivot on the floor, holding the free end with both hands, one cupped over the other, at the upper chest
landmine-press.start: bar end held in both hands at the upper chest, elbows bent and tucked in close to the ribs
landmine-press.end: both arms pressed up and forward along the bar's arc to full extension, the bar end in front of and above the forehead, the torso still
landmine-press.path: a curved arrow beside the bar end: its tail at the hands at the upper chest and its head pointing UP and to the RIGHT of the picture (forward, the way the chest faces, toward the side of the bar's floor pivot), following the bar's arc; it never curls back over the head
landmine-press.seqNote: in both panels the mannequin faces the RIGHT of the picture and the bar's other end sits in its pivot on the floor at the lower RIGHT, so the bar slopes down and to the right from the hands; in the RIGHT panel the arms reach up and forward to the right along the bar, the bar end above and in front of the forehead

standing-barbell-overhead-press.name: Standing barbell overhead press
standing-barbell-overhead-press.setup: standing tall, feet hip-width, bar resting on the front of the shoulders, hands just outside shoulder width
standing-barbell-overhead-press.start: bar at the top of the chest at collarbone height, elbows slightly in front of the bar
standing-barbell-overhead-press.end: bar pressed straight overhead, arms straight, head moved slightly forward through the arms, body upright
standing-barbell-overhead-press.path: straight up, close to the face, from the collarbones to overhead

machine-lateral-raise.name: Lateral raise machine
machine-lateral-raise.sideCamera: straight rear view: the camera directly behind the seated mannequin, which faces the machine, so the angle of the upper arms out to the sides reads clearly
machine-lateral-raise.machine: a seated pin-loaded lateral raise machine: a seat facing a padded chest rest, two padded lever arms at the sides whose round pads rest against the outside of the upper arms just above the elbows, the lever pivots level with the shoulders, a weight stack in front
machine-lateral-raise.setup: seat set so the shoulders line up with the lever pivots; chest against the chest rest, feet flat; the pads against the outside of the upper arms, elbows bent about 90 degrees, hands lightly on the handles
machine-lateral-raise.start: upper arms down at the sides, elbows bent, pads resting on the outer upper arms
machine-lateral-raise.end: upper arms raised out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows leading, shoulders down and not shrugged
machine-lateral-raise.path: the elbows travel up and out to the sides in an arc to shoulder height
machine-lateral-raise.hard: the top: upper arms horizontal at shoulder height out to the sides, elbows bent, shoulders down and not shrugged, chest on the chest rest
machine-lateral-raise.seqNote: the two padded lever arms are mirror images and each pivots right behind its own shoulder joint in both panels: each lever runs from that pivot to the round pad on the outside of the upper arm and the handle beside it; nothing reaches across the picture to the frame

cable-lateral-raise.name: Cable lateral raise
cable-lateral-raise.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at the LOWEST position and a single stirrup handle
cable-lateral-raise.setup: standing side-on to the low pulley, holding the handle in the far hand so the cable crosses in front of the body; the near hand on the column
cable-lateral-raise.start: working arm hanging across the front of the hips, elbow softly bent
cable-lateral-raise.end: working arm raised out to the side to shoulder height, elbow slightly bent and level with the hand
cable-lateral-raise.path: an upward arc out to the side from the front of the hips to shoulder height
cable-lateral-raise.machineNote: the cable leaves the column through the pulley on the carriage near the floor and the stirrup handle hangs right at that low pulley; no cable runs down from the top of the column to the handle

dumbbell-lateral-raise.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
dumbbell-lateral-raise.setup: standing tall, feet hip-width, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, elbows softly bent
dumbbell-lateral-raise.start: arms hanging at the sides, dumbbells beside the thighs
dumbbell-lateral-raise.end: arms raised out to the sides to shoulder height, elbows slightly above the wrists, palms down
dumbbell-lateral-raise.path: upward arcs out to both sides to shoulder height

band-lateral-raise.name: Band lateral raise
band-lateral-raise.setup: standing on the middle of a resistance band, feet hip-width, an end of the band in each hand at the sides
band-lateral-raise.start: arms hanging at the sides, band taut
band-lateral-raise.end: arms raised out to the sides to shoulder height, band stretched
band-lateral-raise.path: one arrow beside each hand, curving up and out to the side to shoulder height
band-lateral-raise.seqNote: the resistance band is light grey like a cable, never orange; its middle runs under both feet and one end goes up to each hand

reverse-pec-deck.name: Reverse pec deck (rear delt fly machine)
reverse-pec-deck.machine: a pec deck and rear delt machine set for reverse flyes: a seat facing a tall chest pad, two swinging arms with handles in front of the pad at shoulder height, a weight stack
reverse-pec-deck.setup: seat set so the handles are at shoulder height; chest against the pad; arms straight forward holding the handles, palms facing each other or down
reverse-pec-deck.start: arms extended straight forward at shoulder height, hands close together
reverse-pec-deck.end: arms swept out and back in a wide arc until in line with the shoulders, elbows softly bent, shoulder blades squeezed
reverse-pec-deck.path: a single curved arrow beside the hand on the right of the picture, curving outward and back from in front of the chest to the side at shoulder height, its head pointing away from the body

rear-delt-dumbbell-fly.name: Rear delt dumbbell fly
rear-delt-dumbbell-fly.setup: lying face down on a bench set to about 30 degrees incline (chest supported), a dumbbell in each hand hanging below the shoulders
rear-delt-dumbbell-fly.start: arms hanging straight down under the shoulders, palms facing each other, elbows softly bent
rear-delt-dumbbell-fly.end: arms raised out to the sides to shoulder level, elbows softly bent
rear-delt-dumbbell-fly.path: a single curved arrow beside one hand, rising up and out to the side, its head pointing up and away from the body

cable-rear-delt-fly.name: Cable rear delt fly
cable-rear-delt-fly.machine: a dual-pulley cable crossover station with both pulley carriages at shoulder height and no handles, the cable ends held directly
cable-rear-delt-fly.setup: standing centred, holding the left cable in the right hand and the right cable in the left hand, the cables crossed in front of the chest
cable-rear-delt-fly.start: arms crossed in front of the chest at shoulder height
cable-rear-delt-fly.end: arms swept out and back to a T at shoulder height, elbows softly bent
cable-rear-delt-fly.path: one arrow beside each hand, each starting at that hand in front of the chest and curving outward and back to the side at shoulder height, the two heads pointing away from each other, toward the two columns
cable-rear-delt-fly.seqNote: the two cables cross IN FRONT of the chest, hidden by the torso in this rear view: the cable from the LEFT pulley runs to the mannequin's RIGHT hand and the cable from the RIGHT pulley to its LEFT hand; no cable crosses the back, the shoulders or the neck; in the RIGHT panel each hand still grips its own cable end, out to the side level with the shoulder and well inside the columns, and the hands never hold the frame
cable-rear-delt-fly.machineNote: each cable hangs on its own from its own pulley carriage and ends in a small ball stop just below the pulley, with no handle; the two cables are separate and never meet, cross or span the gap between the columns

face-pull.name: Face pull
face-pull.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at about forehead height and a rope attachment with two knotted ends
face-pull.setup: standing tall facing the pulley in a slight split stance, a step back so the cable is taut and the arms are straight; an overhand grip on the two rope ends, palms down, one end in each hand
face-pull.start: arms extended forward toward the pulley at face height
face-pull.end: rope pulled to the face, the two ends split apart beside the ears, elbows high and level with the shoulders, forearms pointing up, upper arms rotated back
face-pull.path: a straight arrow beside the forearms running from the pulley side back toward the face, its head next to the face (the way the rope travels when pulled)
face-pull.hard: the end of the pull: rope at the face with the hands beside the ears, elbows high at shoulder level and slightly behind the torso, forearms vertical, chest up
face-pull.machineNote: a single upright column with a vertical row of adjustment holes and a pulley carriage clamped at about the forehead height of a standing adult, the rope hanging from that carriage's pulley; NO seat, NO bench, NO top beam reaching forward

band-pull-apart.name: Band pull-apart
band-pull-apart.setup: standing tall, holding a resistance band with both hands about shoulder width apart, straight arms out in front at shoulder height
band-pull-apart.start: arms straight out in front at shoulder height, band slack
band-pull-apart.end: band pulled apart until the arms are out to the sides at shoulder height and the band touches the chest
band-pull-apart.path: one arrow beside each hand, each curving outward and back from in front of the chest to the side at shoulder height, the two heads pointing away from each other
band-pull-apart.seqNote: the resistance band is light grey like a cable, never orange, and it stays in FRONT of the body: in the LEFT panel it stretches between the hands in front of the shoulders; in the RIGHT panel it lies across the front of the chest, so from behind only its two ends show at the hands; it never crosses the back, the neck or the shoulder blades

cable-external-rotation.name: Cable external rotation
cable-external-rotation.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at elbow height and a single stirrup handle
cable-external-rotation.setup: standing side-on to the column with the working arm farthest from it; elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to the side with a small rolled towel between elbow and ribs; the handle held across the belly
cable-external-rotation.start: forearm across the belly, elbow bent 90 degrees at the side
cable-external-rotation.end: forearm rotated outward away from the body as far as is comfortable, elbow still pinned to the side
cable-external-rotation.path: a curved arrow just below the moving forearm: its tail starts at the hand in front of the belly and it curves outward to the LEFT, toward the left edge of the picture and away from the cable column, its head pointing left: the hand swings outward around the pinned elbow
cable-external-rotation.seqNote: the mannequin faces the camera; the cable column stands at the RIGHT edge of the picture beside it; the working arm is the mannequin's arm on the LEFT of the picture (the one farthest from the column), its elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to the side with a small rolled towel; the cable runs from the column across the front of the belly to the handle in that hand; the other arm hangs relaxed; in the RIGHT panel that forearm points out to the LEFT, away from the column, the elbow still at the side

side-lying-external-rotation.name: Side-lying external rotation
side-lying-external-rotation.setup: lying on one side on a flat bench, head resting on the lower arm, the top arm's elbow bent 90 degrees and resting on the side with a small rolled towel under it, a light dumbbell in the top hand
side-lying-external-rotation.end: forearm rotated up until it points toward the ceiling, elbow still on the side
side-lying-external-rotation.path: a curved arrow from the hand resting on the belly up around the elbow, its head pointing straight up at the ceiling above the elbow
side-lying-external-rotation.seqNote: the mannequin lies on its side facing the camera, the head at the LEFT end of the bench resting on the lower arm; the top arm's upper arm lies flat along the top of the ribcage, horizontal in the picture, from the shoulder next to the head to the elbow at the waist, and a small rolled towel sits on top of the ribs between that elbow and the body, not under the body; in both panels the upper arm, the elbow and the towel do not move; in the LEFT panel the forearm lies across the belly holding the dumbbell; in the RIGHT panel only the forearm has turned up: it points straight up at the ceiling from the elbow at the waist, so the dumbbell is straight above the waist, in the middle of the body's length, never above the shoulder or the head

band-external-rotation.name: Band external rotation
band-external-rotation.setup: standing side-on to a resistance band anchored at elbow height, the working arm farthest from the anchor, elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to the side
band-external-rotation.start: forearm across the belly holding the band
band-external-rotation.end: forearm rotated outward away from the body, elbow still at the side
band-external-rotation.path: a curved arrow just below the moving forearm: its tail starts at the hand in front of the belly and it curves outward to the RIGHT, away from the anchor post, its head pointing right
band-external-rotation.seqNote: the resistance band is light grey like a cable, never orange; the mannequin faces the camera; the band's anchor post stands at the LEFT edge of the picture and the working arm is the mannequin's arm on the RIGHT of the picture (the one farthest from the anchor), its elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to the side; the band runs from the post across the front of the belly to that hand; the other arm hangs relaxed

machine-shrug.name: Shrug machine
machine-shrug.machine: a plate-loaded standing shrug machine: a platform to stand on between two handles at hip height at the ends of a lever arm, weight plates on horns at the lever ends
machine-shrug.setup: standing tall on the platform between the handles, arms straight down holding the handles
machine-shrug.start: shoulders relaxed and low, arms straight
machine-shrug.end: shoulders raised straight up toward the ears, arms still straight

dumbbell-shrug.name: Dumbbell shrug
dumbbell-shrug.setup: standing tall, a heavy dumbbell in each hand at the sides
dumbbell-shrug.start: shoulders relaxed and low, arms straight
dumbbell-shrug.end: shoulders raised straight up toward the ears, arms still straight

vertical-traction.name: Vertical traction (lever pulldown) machine
vertical-traction.machine: a seated pin-loaded vertical traction machine: a seat with padded knee rollers on a short post at the front end of the seat, resting on top of the thighs just behind the knees (in a profile view: a round pad seen end-on, sitting on top of the thigh near the knee, never behind the hips), two independent handle arms above the head that pull down in an arc (no bar and no cable at the hands), a weight stack
vertical-traction.setup: seat set so the thighs fit snugly under the pads and the handles are just reachable with straight arms; feet flat
vertical-traction.start: arms extended up gripping the handles, shoulders reaching up, torso upright
vertical-traction.end: handles pulled down to the shoulders, elbows down beside the ribs and slightly back, chest up
vertical-traction.path: down and slightly back in an arc from overhead to the shoulders

lat-pulldown.name: Lat pulldown
lat-pulldown.machine: a lat pulldown station: a tall frame whose weight stack column stands in front of the seated mannequin (on the right in a profile view), a top beam reaching back from the column to a pulley just above and in front of the mannequin's head, the cable running from that pulley straight down to the middle of a long straight bar with slightly bent ends, and a seat with padded knee rollers on a short post at the front end of the seat, resting on top of the thighs just behind the knees (in a profile view: a round pad seen end-on, sitting on top of the thigh near the knee, never behind the hips)
lat-pulldown.setup: seated facing the weight stack column, thighs locked under the knee rollers, feet flat; overhand grip on the bar about one and a half times shoulder width (in this profile view the bar is seen end-on, as a short stub held in the hands)
lat-pulldown.start: arms fully extended overhead holding the bar above and slightly in front of the head, torso upright with a slight lean back of about 10 to 15 degrees, shoulders reaching up; the cable is long and straight from the pulley to the bar
lat-pulldown.end: bar pulled down IN FRONT of the face to the top of the chest at collarbone height (never behind the neck), elbows pointing down and slightly back beside the ribs, forearms vertical under the bar, chest lifted toward the bar; the torso keeps the same slight lean and the thighs stay under the rollers
lat-pulldown.path: straight down in front of the face from overhead to the upper chest
lat-pulldown.hard: the bottom of the pull: bar at the upper chest, elbows down beside the ribs and slightly behind the torso, forearms vertical under the bar, chest up, torso leaning back only about 10 to 15 degrees, thighs under the rollers
lat-pulldown.note: the weight stack column stands on the RIGHT, in front of the mannequin, which faces it; the top beam reaches back from that column over the mannequin's head to the pulley; no part of the frame stands behind the mannequin's back; the knee roller is a round pad seen end-on resting on top of the thigh just behind the knee, never at the hip or behind the buttocks

plate-loaded-pulldown.name: Plate-loaded pulldown
plate-loaded-pulldown.machine: a plate-loaded front lat pulldown: a seat with padded knee rollers on a short post at the front end of the seat, resting on top of the thighs just behind the knees (in a profile view: a round pad seen end-on, sitting on top of the thigh near the knee, never behind the hips), two independent lever arms with handles overhead that pull down and back in an arc, weight plates on horns at the back of the levers
plate-loaded-pulldown.setup: thighs locked under the pads, feet flat; hands on the overhead handles
plate-loaded-pulldown.start: arms extended up holding the handles, shoulders reaching up
plate-loaded-pulldown.end: handles pulled down to the upper chest, elbows down and back beside the ribs, chest up
plate-loaded-pulldown.path: down and slightly back in an arc to the upper chest

neutral-grip-pulldown.name: Neutral-grip pulldown
neutral-grip-pulldown.machine: a lat pulldown station with a parallel-grip handle (two handles with the palms facing each other, about shoulder width apart) on the high pulley, the weight stack column in front of the seated mannequin, and a seat with padded knee rollers on a short post at the front end of the seat, resting on top of the thighs just behind the knees (in a profile view: a round pad seen end-on, sitting on top of the thigh near the knee, never behind the hips)
neutral-grip-pulldown.setup: seated facing the weight stack column, thighs locked under the knee rollers, feet flat; palms facing each other on the parallel handles
neutral-grip-pulldown.start: arms fully extended overhead, torso upright with a slight lean back
neutral-grip-pulldown.end: handle pulled down to the upper chest, elbows down beside the ribs, chest up
neutral-grip-pulldown.path: straight down in front of the face to the upper chest

assisted-pull-up.name: Assisted pull-up
assisted-pull-up.machine: an assisted pull-up and dip machine: a tall frame with wide overhand handles and parallel handles on top, dip handles lower at the sides, a padded knee platform on a lever linked to a weight stack that pushes up to help, steps to climb on
assisted-pull-up.setup: kneeling with both knees on the assistance pad, hands on the top handles a little wider than the shoulders, overhand grip
assisted-pull-up.start: hanging with straight arms overhead, body upright, knees on the pad, shoulders reaching up
assisted-pull-up.end: body pulled up until the chin is level with the handles, elbows bent sharply and down beside the ribs, chest toward the handles, knees still on the pad
assisted-pull-up.path: the whole body rises straight up
assisted-pull-up.hard: the top of the pull: chin level with the handles, elbows bent sharply and down beside the ribs, chest up toward the handles, knees on the pad

single-arm-cable-pulldown.name: Single-arm cable pulldown
single-arm-cable-pulldown.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at the TOP and a single stirrup handle
single-arm-cable-pulldown.setup: kneeling on one knee below the high pulley, the working arm reaching up holding the handle
single-arm-cable-pulldown.start: working arm extended overhead, shoulder reaching up
single-arm-cable-pulldown.end: handle pulled down to the side of the chest, elbow down beside the ribs
single-arm-cable-pulldown.path: straight down from overhead to the side of the chest

band-assisted-pull-up.name: Band-assisted pull-up
band-assisted-pull-up.setup: a long loop resistance band hooked over a pull-up bar, one knee resting in the band's loop, hands on the bar a little wider than the shoulders with an overhand grip
band-assisted-pull-up.start: hanging with straight arms, knee in the band
band-assisted-pull-up.end: chin above the bar, elbows down beside the ribs, chest toward the bar
band-assisted-pull-up.path: the whole body rises straight up

pull-up.name: Pull-up
pull-up.setup: hanging from a pull-up bar, overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders, legs straight or knees slightly bent
pull-up.end: chin over the bar, elbows down and back beside the ribs, chest toward the bar
pull-up.path: the whole body rises straight up

chin-up.name: Chin-up
chin-up.setup: hanging from a pull-up bar, underhand grip (palms facing you) at shoulder width
chin-up.end: chin over the bar, elbows down in front of the ribs, chest toward the bar
chin-up.path: the whole body rises straight up

machine-pullover.name: Pullover machine
machine-pullover.machine: a seated pin-loaded pullover machine: a seat with a back pad and a hip belt, a curved bar above the head joined to padded elbow plates on a lever that rotates around the shoulders, a weight stack
machine-pullover.setup: seat set so the shoulders line up with the lever's pivot; belt across the hips; elbows against the pads, hands resting lightly on the bar
machine-pullover.start: arms raised overhead and slightly behind the head, elbows on the pads, a stretch along the sides of the back
machine-pullover.end: arms rotated forward and down in a big arc until the bar touches the belly
machine-pullover.path: a large downward arc around the shoulders from overhead to the belly

straight-arm-pulldown.name: Straight-arm pulldown
straight-arm-pulldown.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at the TOP and a straight bar attachment
straight-arm-pulldown.setup: standing a step back from the high pulley, feet hip-width, hips hinged slightly forward with a flat back, arms straight holding the bar at shoulder width
straight-arm-pulldown.start: arms straight up in front at about head height, a stretch along the sides of the back
straight-arm-pulldown.end: bar swept down in an arc to the thighs, arms still straight
straight-arm-pulldown.path: a downward arc with straight arms from head height to the thighs

dumbbell-pullover.name: Dumbbell pullover
dumbbell-pullover.setup: lying on the back along a flat bench, feet flat on the floor, holding one dumbbell with both hands above the chest, elbows softly bent
dumbbell-pullover.start: arms lowered back behind the head in an arc, the dumbbell about level with the bench, a stretch through the sides and the chest
dumbbell-pullover.end: dumbbell brought back up over the chest in the same arc
dumbbell-pullover.path: an upward arc from behind the head to over the chest

machine-row.name: Seated row machine (chest-supported)
machine-row.machine: a seated pin-loaded row machine: a seat, an upright padded chest rest in front, two handles on lever arms reaching forward with horizontal and vertical grips, a weight stack
machine-row.setup: seat set so the handles are level with the lower chest; chest rest set so the arms are fully stretched at the handles; chest against the pad, feet flat
machine-row.start: arms extended forward holding the handles, shoulder blades spread forward, chest on the pad
machine-row.end: handles pulled back to the sides of the lower ribs, elbows driven back past the torso, shoulder blades squeezed together, chest still on the pad
machine-row.path: a straight arrow just below the forearms, its tail at the handles and its head pointing LEFT toward the lower ribs and the seat (toward the left edge of the picture, away from the weight stack): the hands travel back toward the body
machine-row.hard: the end of the pull: handles beside the lower ribs, elbows behind the torso and close to the sides, shoulder blades squeezed, chest on the pad, torso upright
machine-row.machineNote: the chest pad stands upright at the front edge of the seat, facing the seat; the two handles sit on the FAR side of the chest pad (between the pad and the weight stack) at chest height, so a user on the seat leans the chest on the pad and reaches past it to the handles; seen from the seat side at three-quarter, so the seat, then the pad, then the handles beyond it read in that order
machine-row.seqNote: seen as a true profile: the seat on the left, the vertical chest pad standing just in front of the mannequin's chest, the two handles on the far side of that pad (between the pad and the weight stack) at lower-chest height; the chest stays pressed on the pad in both panels; in the RIGHT panel the hands are pulled back to beside the lower ribs at the sides of the pad and the elbows point straight BACK, clearly behind the back line of the torso

plate-loaded-row.name: Plate-loaded row
plate-loaded-row.machine: a plate-loaded iso-lateral row: a seat and an upright chest pad, two independent lever arms with handles reaching forward, weight plates on horns on the levers
plate-loaded-row.setup: chest against the pad, feet flat; hands on the handles
plate-loaded-row.start: arms extended forward, shoulder blades spread
plate-loaded-row.end: handles pulled back to the ribs, elbows behind the torso, shoulder blades squeezed
plate-loaded-row.path: back and slightly down in an arc to the ribs (toward the left of the picture, toward the mannequin's back)

t-bar-row.name: Chest-supported T-bar row
t-bar-row.machine: a chest-supported T-bar row: a foot platform, an inclined chest pad, a long lever arm under the pad with wide and narrow handles, weight plates on a horn at the end of the lever
t-bar-row.setup: standing on the foot platform with the chest on the inclined pad, arms hanging straight down holding the handles
t-bar-row.start: arms straight down holding the handles, shoulder blades spread
t-bar-row.end: handles pulled up to the lower chest, elbows back past the torso, shoulder blades squeezed
t-bar-row.path: straight up from the hanging position to the lower chest
t-bar-row.machineNote: one long lever arm pivots at floor level at the BACK end, just in front of the foot platform, runs forward under the chest pad and ends in the plate horn at the FRONT; the wide and narrow handles are fixed on that lever just below the front edge of the chest pad, within arm's reach of someone lying on the pad; nothing else: no seat, no stool and no second post with handles

chest-supported-dumbbell-row.name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
chest-supported-dumbbell-row.setup: lying face down on a bench set to about 30 to 45 degrees incline, feet on the floor, a dumbbell in each hand hanging straight down
chest-supported-dumbbell-row.start: arms hanging straight below the shoulders
chest-supported-dumbbell-row.end: dumbbells rowed up to the sides of the lower ribs, elbows behind the torso
chest-supported-dumbbell-row.path: straight up from below the shoulders to the lower ribs

high-row-machine.name: High row machine
high-row-machine.machine: a plate-loaded high row: a seat with a thigh pad and a chest pad, two independent lever arms with handles high in front that pull down and back in an arc, weight plates on horns on the levers
high-row-machine.setup: thighs under the pad, chest against the pad; arms reaching up and forward to the handles
high-row-machine.start: arms extended up and forward holding the handles
high-row-machine.end: handles pulled down and back to the shoulders, elbows behind the torso
high-row-machine.path: down and back in an arc to the shoulders (down and toward the left of the picture, toward the mannequin's back)

seated-cable-row.name: Seated cable row
seated-cable-row.machine: a seated cable row (low row) station: a long low bench, an angled foot platform, a low pulley at foot level with a close-grip V-handle (two parallel grips), a weight stack at the far end
seated-cable-row.setup: sitting on the bench, feet on the platform, knees softly bent, torso upright; both hands on the V-handle with the palms facing each other
seated-cable-row.start: arms extended forward toward the pulley, shoulder blades spread, torso upright and leaning forward no more than slightly
seated-cable-row.end: handle pulled to the belly just below the ribs, elbows driven back close to the sides, shoulder blades squeezed, torso upright and still
seated-cable-row.path: straight back from the pulley to the belly
seated-cable-row.hard: the end of the pull: handle at the belly, elbows behind the torso close to the sides, shoulder blades squeezed, torso upright at about 90 degrees to the bench, knees softly bent

inverted-row.name: Inverted row
inverted-row.setup: lying under a bar fixed at about hip height (a Smith machine or rack), hands on the bar a little wider than the shoulders, heels on the floor, body straight
inverted-row.start: hanging under the bar with straight arms, body one straight line from heels to head
inverted-row.end: chest pulled up to the bar, elbows back, body still straight
inverted-row.path: the straight body rises toward the bar, pivoting on the heels

single-arm-cable-row.name: Single-arm cable row
single-arm-cable-row.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at chest height and a single stirrup handle
single-arm-cable-row.setup: standing facing the pulley in a split stance, the working hand on the handle, the other hand on the hip
single-arm-cable-row.start: working arm extended forward toward the pulley, shoulder reaching forward
single-arm-cable-row.end: handle pulled to the side of the ribs, elbow back past the torso, torso not rotating
single-arm-cable-row.path: straight back from the pulley to the side of the ribs (toward the left of the picture, toward the mannequin's back)

single-arm-dumbbell-row.name: Single-arm dumbbell row
single-arm-dumbbell-row.setup: one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, back flat and nearly parallel to the floor, the other foot on the floor, a dumbbell hanging in the free hand
single-arm-dumbbell-row.start: arm hanging straight down below the shoulder
single-arm-dumbbell-row.end: dumbbell rowed up to the hip, elbow close to the body and behind the torso
single-arm-dumbbell-row.path: up and slightly back from below the shoulder to the hip

barbell-row.name: Barbell bent-over row
barbell-row.setup: standing with feet hip-width, hinged forward at the hips to about 45 degrees with a flat back and soft knees, overhand grip a little wider than the shoulders
barbell-row.start: bar hanging at arm's length below the knees, back flat
barbell-row.end: bar rowed to the lower ribs, elbows back past the torso, back still flat and at the same angle
barbell-row.path: straight up from below the knees to the lower ribs

lower-back-machine.name: Lower back machine (lumbar extension)
lower-back-machine.machine: a seated pin-loaded lower back machine: a seat with a foot platform, thigh and hip pads that lock the pelvis, a padded roller across the upper back on a lever arm pivoting at the level of the lower back, a weight stack
lower-back-machine.setup: seat set so the machine's pivot lines up with the lower back at navel height; feet on the platform, thigh pads locked; upper back against the roller, arms crossed on the chest
lower-back-machine.start: torso leaning forward about 30 to 40 degrees, the back gently rounded forward against the roller
lower-back-machine.end: torso pushed back to upright, spine extended to neutral, hips still locked
lower-back-machine.path: a curved arrow in the empty space behind the upper back, between the back and the weight stack: its tail starts beside the roller and it curves UP and to the LEFT, toward the top-left corner of the picture (toward the weight stack side), its head at its upper-left end; the roller and the upper back travel up and backward as the trunk comes upright; the arrow never points right, forward or over the head
lower-back-machine.hard: the forward position: torso leaning forward about 40 degrees against the roller, pelvis locked by the pads, feet flat on the platform, arms crossed on the chest
lower-back-machine.sideNote: the mannequin SITS: the buttocks rest fully on the seat, the thighs lie level on the seat locked under the thigh pads, the knees are bent about 90 degrees with the feet on the platform; only the trunk leans forward from the hips against the roller
lower-back-machine.sidePath: a curved arrow in the empty space behind the upper back, between the back and the weight stack: its tail starts beside the roller and it curves UP and to the LEFT, toward the top-left corner of the picture (toward the weight stack side), its head at its upper-left end; the roller and the upper back travel up and backward as the trunk comes upright; the arrow never points right, forward or over the head

back-extension-45.name: 45-degree back extension
back-extension-45.machine: a 45-degree back extension bench (hyperextension): an angled frame with a padded thigh support and two ankle rollers on a foot plate, no weights
back-extension-45.setup: on the 45-degree bench with the thighs on the pad, its top edge just below the hip crease, ankles locked under the rollers, arms crossed on the chest
back-extension-45.start: torso hanging down toward the floor, hips bent, back flat
back-extension-45.end: torso raised until the body forms one straight line from head to heels, not beyond
back-extension-45.path: a curved arrow just beyond the head and shoulders, arcing around the hips: its tail starts at the hanging head below and to the right of the hip pad, it bulges out to the right and curves UP, and its head points up toward the upper RIGHT of the picture where the head ends in line with the legs; it never continues past that line toward the feet or the upper left
back-extension-45.seqNote: in both panels the foot plate and ankle rollers are at the LOWER LEFT and the hip pad in the middle, so the legs slope up to the right; in the RIGHT panel the head is at the upper RIGHT and the body is one straight diagonal line from the heels through the hips to the head, never arched back

reverse-hyperextension.name: Reverse hyperextension
reverse-hyperextension.setup: lying face down on a high flat bench with the hips at the end of the bench, holding the sides of the bench, legs hanging down
reverse-hyperextension.start: legs hanging down toward the floor, hips bent
reverse-hyperextension.end: straight legs raised behind until in line with the torso
reverse-hyperextension.path: a curved arrow beside the feet that swings them up and BACK, away from the bench, until the legs are level with the body (toward the upper left of the picture when the head is on the right), its head pointing up and back

four-way-neck-machine.name: 4-way neck machine
four-way-neck-machine.machine: a seated pin-loaded 4-way neck machine: a seat with a torso pad, a padded head plate on a lever arm at head height that can face front, back or sides, side handles, a weight stack
four-way-neck-machine.setup: seated facing away from the head pad so the back of the head rests on it, torso upright, hands on the side handles
four-way-neck-machine.start: head tilted slightly forward, chin toward the chest, back of the head against the pad
four-way-neck-machine.end: head pushed back to neutral and slightly beyond against the pad, torso still
four-way-neck-machine.path: the head moves back in a small arc against the pad

neck-extension.name: Neck extension
neck-extension.setup: lying face down on a flat bench with the head and neck over the end, both hands holding a light weight plate on a folded towel against the back of the head
neck-extension.start: head lowered, chin toward the chest
neck-extension.end: head raised until it is in line with the body
neck-extension.path: the head rises in a small arc

neck-flexion.name: Neck flexion
neck-flexion.setup: lying face up on a flat bench with the head over the end, both hands holding a light weight plate on a folded towel on the forehead
neck-flexion.start: head relaxed back level with the bench, hanging just beyond its LEFT end
neck-flexion.end: chin tucked toward the chest and the head lifted, the shoulders and upper back still flat on the bench
neck-flexion.path: the head curls up in a small arc
neck-flexion.seqNote: the flat bench ends at the top of the shoulders: the whole head is beyond the LEFT end of the bench, unsupported, in both panels; the shoulder blades and the upper back stay pressed flat on the bench pad in both panels and the chest never lifts; the elbows point up and the upper arms rest on the chest; the movement is only a nod of the head: in the LEFT panel the head hangs back level with the bench, in the RIGHT panel the head has tilted up so the chin moves toward the chest; never a sit-up or a crunch

neck-isometrics.name: Neck isometrics
neck-isometrics.setup: seated tall on a bench, neck neutral; one palm presses against the head while the neck resists without moving
neck-isometrics.start: palm on the forehead pressing back, head still and neutral
neck-isometrics.end: palm on the side of the head pressing sideways, head still and neutral
neck-isometrics.path: a short straight arrow at the palm showing it pressing into the forehead while the head does not move

machine-preacher-curl.name: Machine preacher curl
machine-preacher-curl.machine: a seated pin-loaded preacher curl (arm curl) machine: a seat, an angled arm pad in front sloping down away from the body, two handles on a lever whose pivot sits level with the elbows, a weight stack
machine-preacher-curl.setup: seat set so the armpits sit snugly at the top of the arm pad and the elbows line up with the machine's pivot; upper arms flat on the pad; underhand grip on the handles
machine-preacher-curl.start: arms almost straight along the pad, elbows slightly bent, handles low
machine-preacher-curl.end: elbows fully bent, handles raised toward the shoulders, upper arms still flat on the pad
machine-preacher-curl.path: the hands curl up in an arc around the elbows
machine-preacher-curl.hard: early in the curl: forearms about level with the floor, elbows bent about 45 degrees from straight, upper arms flat on the pad, armpits snug against its top

incline-dumbbell-curl.name: Incline dumbbell curl
incline-dumbbell-curl.setup: lying back on a bench set to about 45 to 60 degrees incline, arms hanging straight down behind the torso line, a dumbbell in each hand, palms forward
incline-dumbbell-curl.start: arms hanging straight down from the shoulders
incline-dumbbell-curl.end: dumbbells curled up toward the shoulders, upper arms still hanging vertically
incline-dumbbell-curl.path: the hands curl up in an arc around the elbows

bayesian-cable-curl.name: Bayesian cable curl
bayesian-cable-curl.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set LOW, at about knee height, and a single stirrup handle
bayesian-cable-curl.setup: standing facing away from the column in a split stance, the working arm extended down and behind the body holding the handle, palm forward
bayesian-cable-curl.start: working arm extended down and slightly behind the torso, a stretch in the biceps
bayesian-cable-curl.end: handle curled up toward the shoulder, the upper arm still behind the torso line
bayesian-cable-curl.path: the hand curls forward and up in an arc around the elbow
bayesian-cable-curl.seqNote: the cable column stands on the LEFT of each panel, BEHIND the mannequin, which faces the right edge with its back to the column; the cable runs from the low pulley behind the mannequin forward and up to the hand at its side, never between the legs; in the LEFT panel the working arm hangs slightly BEHIND the hip, drawn back by the cable; in the RIGHT panel the forearm is curled up to the front of the shoulder while the upper arm still points down and slightly back

ez-bar-preacher-curl.name: EZ-bar preacher curl
ez-bar-preacher-curl.setup: seated at a preacher bench, upper arms on the angled pad, an EZ curl bar held underhand on its angled grips
ez-bar-preacher-curl.start: arms almost straight along the pad
ez-bar-preacher-curl.end: bar curled up toward the shoulders, upper arms still on the pad
ez-bar-preacher-curl.path: the bar curls up in an arc around the elbows

cable-curl.name: Cable curl
cable-curl.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage at the LOWEST position and a short straight bar attachment
cable-curl.setup: standing facing the pulley, feet hip-width, underhand grip on the bar at shoulder width, elbows at the sides
cable-curl.start: arms straight down, bar at the thighs
cable-curl.end: bar curled up to the shoulders, elbows still at the sides
cable-curl.path: the bar curls up in an arc around the elbows

dumbbell-curl.name: Dumbbell curl
dumbbell-curl.setup: standing tall, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, palms forward
dumbbell-curl.start: arms straight down at the sides
dumbbell-curl.end: dumbbells curled to the shoulders, elbows still at the sides
dumbbell-curl.path: the hands curl up in an arc around the elbows
dumbbell-curl.seqNote: an underhand grip: the palms face forward in the LEFT panel and up toward the shoulders in the RIGHT panel, so each dumbbell's handle runs across the body from side to side, never front to back like a hammer curl; the elbows stay pinned at the sides of the ribs in both panels

barbell-curl.name: Barbell curl
barbell-curl.setup: standing tall, underhand grip on a barbell at shoulder width, elbows at the sides
barbell-curl.start: bar at the thighs, arms straight
barbell-curl.end: bar curled to the shoulders, elbows still at the sides
barbell-curl.path: the bar curls up in an arc around the elbows

hammer-curl.name: Hammer curl
hammer-curl.setup: standing tall, a dumbbell in each hand at the sides with the palms facing the thighs (neutral grip, thumbs forward)
hammer-curl.start: arms straight down at the sides, palms facing the thighs
hammer-curl.end: dumbbells curled up to the shoulders keeping the thumbs up and the palms facing each other, elbows still at the sides
hammer-curl.path: the hands curl up in an arc around the elbows
hammer-curl.hard: the middle of the curl: elbows bent 90 degrees at the sides, forearms level with the floor, thumbs up, upper arms vertical

reverse-curl.name: Reverse curl
reverse-curl.setup: standing tall, overhand grip (palms down) on an EZ bar or barbell at shoulder width, elbows at the sides
reverse-curl.start: bar at the thighs, arms straight, palms facing back
reverse-curl.end: bar curled to the shoulders with the palms still down
reverse-curl.path: the bar curls up in an arc around the elbows

overhead-cable-triceps-extension.name: Overhead cable triceps extension
overhead-cable-triceps-extension.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at about head height and a rope attachment
overhead-cable-triceps-extension.setup: standing in a split stance facing away from the column, leaning slightly forward, holding the rope behind the head with both hands, upper arms beside the head pointing forward and up
overhead-cable-triceps-extension.start: elbows bent fully, hands behind the head, a stretch along the back of the upper arms
overhead-cable-triceps-extension.end: arms extended forward and up in line with the upper arms, elbows straight, upper arms unmoved
overhead-cable-triceps-extension.path: a curved arrow from behind the head that swings the hands forward and up, AWAY from the column (toward the right of the picture), its head pointing forward-up beyond the forehead

machine-triceps-extension.name: Triceps extension machine
machine-triceps-extension.machine: a seated pin-loaded triceps extension machine: a seat, an angled arm pad in front, two handles on a lever whose pivot sits level with the elbows, a weight stack
machine-triceps-extension.setup: seat set so the elbows line up with the machine's pivot, upper arms flat on the pad, hands on the handles
machine-triceps-extension.start: elbows bent about 90 degrees or more, hands near the shoulders
machine-triceps-extension.end: arms extended straight along the pad, upper arms unmoved
machine-triceps-extension.path: the hands push forward and down in an arc around the elbows

dumbbell-overhead-triceps-extension.name: Dumbbell overhead triceps extension
dumbbell-overhead-triceps-extension.setup: seated on a bench with an upright back rest, holding one dumbbell with both hands behind the head, upper arms vertical beside the ears
dumbbell-overhead-triceps-extension.start: elbows bent fully, dumbbell behind the head
dumbbell-overhead-triceps-extension.end: arms extended straight overhead, upper arms unmoved
dumbbell-overhead-triceps-extension.path: the dumbbell rises in an arc around the elbows to overhead

skull-crusher.name: Lying triceps extension (skull crusher)
skull-crusher.setup: lying on a flat bench, feet flat, holding an EZ bar above the chest with the arms angled slightly back toward the head
skull-crusher.start: elbows bent, bar lowered to just above the forehead, upper arms angled slightly back
skull-crusher.end: arms extended, bar above the eyes and shoulders, upper arms unmoved
skull-crusher.path: the bar rises in an arc around the elbows

cable-pushdown.name: Cable triceps pushdown
cable-pushdown.machine: a single cable column with the pulley carriage set at the TOP and a short straight bar attachment
cable-pushdown.setup: standing tall facing the pulley, close to the cable, feet hip-width, a slight forward lean, elbows pinned to the sides; overhand grip on the bar with the hands about 20 to 30 centimetres apart
cable-pushdown.start: elbows bent a little more than 90 degrees, forearms about level with the floor, bar at lower-chest height, upper arms vertical at the sides
cable-pushdown.end: arms pushed straight down, bar at the thighs, elbows still at the sides
cable-pushdown.path: the bar travels down in a short arc around the elbows
cable-pushdown.hard: the middle of the push: elbows bent 90 degrees, forearms level with the floor, upper arms vertical and pinned to the sides, wrists straight
cable-pushdown.sideNote: the cable column stands on the RIGHT of the picture in front of the mannequin, which faces it; the cable hangs from the top pulley straight down in front of the mannequin's face and chest to the bar held in front of the belly; no part of the column stands behind the mannequin and the cable never passes behind or through the body
cable-pushdown.machineNote: a free-standing single cable column with the pulley at the top and the short bar hanging from it; NO seat, NO bench, NO knee rollers — the exercise is done standing

close-grip-bench-press.name: Close-grip bench press
close-grip-bench-press.setup: lying on a flat bench with rack uprights, hands on the bar about shoulder width apart, elbows close to the body
close-grip-bench-press.start: bar lowered to the lower chest, elbows tucked close to the sides
close-grip-bench-press.end: bar pressed up to arm's length
close-grip-bench-press.path: straight up from the lower chest to arm's length

diamond-push-up.name: Diamond push-up
diamond-push-up.setup: push-up position with the hands together under the chest, thumbs touching so the hands frame a diamond-shaped gap, body one straight line
diamond-push-up.start: chest lowered to the hands, elbows close to the body
diamond-push-up.end: arms straight, body still one straight line
diamond-push-up.path: the chest rises straight up while the body pivots on the toes

wrist-curl.name: Wrist curl
wrist-curl.setup: seated on a bench, forearms resting on the thighs palms up, hands hanging over the knees holding dumbbells
wrist-curl.end: wrists curled up as far as possible, forearms still resting on the thighs
wrist-curl.path: the hands curl up in a small arc around the wrists

reverse-wrist-curl.name: Reverse wrist curl
reverse-wrist-curl.setup: seated on a bench, forearms resting on the thighs palms down, hands hanging over the knees holding dumbbells
reverse-wrist-curl.end: backs of the hands raised, wrists extended, forearms still resting
reverse-wrist-curl.path: the hands rise in a small arc around the wrists

farmers-carry.name: Farmer's carry
farmers-carry.setup: standing tall with a heavy dumbbell in each hand at the sides, shoulders level and pulled back
farmers-carry.start: standing tall holding the dumbbells at the sides, about to step off
farmers-carry.end: walking forward mid-stride, torso tall and still, arms straight at the sides, shoulders level
farmers-carry.path: a straight arrow on the floor beside the feet, running from behind the heels to in front of the toes, in the direction the toes point and the mannequin walks
farmers-carry.hard: mid-stride: torso tall and vertical, head over the shoulders over the hips, arms straight at the sides holding the heavy dumbbells, shoulders level and pulled back

dead-hang.name: Dead hang
dead-hang.setup: a pull-up bar overhead, overhand grip at shoulder width
dead-hang.start: standing on a low step under the bar, both hands gripping the bar
dead-hang.end: hanging from the bar with straight arms, feet off the step, shoulders gently engaged
dead-hang.path: a short arrow under the feet showing them lifting off the step
